t: Often called the first global empire, Spain ruled lands across Europe, the Americas, Africa and Asia from the 1490s.
American silver from mines like Potosí reshaped world money, and the Columbian Exchange transformed diets, populations and faiths.
Costly wars and bankruptcies eroded its power; the American colonies broke away by 1826 and the last major ones were lost in 1898.
dyk: From 1565 to 1815 the Manila Galleon linked Acapulco and Manila, the first sustained direct trade link between the Americas and Asia.
ev: Granada falls, ending the Reconquista, and Columbus sails west for Castile
The Treaty of Tordesillas divides the world between Spain and Portugal
Hernán Cortés begins the conquest of the Aztec Empire, completed in 1521
Francisco Pizarro begins the conquest of the Inca Empire
Philip II unites the crowns of Spain and Portugal
The Spanish Armada sent against England is defeated and wrecked by storms
The Peace of Westphalia confirms Dutch independence from Spain
Defeat by the United States strips Spain of Cuba, Puerto Rico and the Philippines

f.predecessor: Crown of Castile, Crown of Aragon
